utility.value: Nevada Power Company d/b/a NV Energy
utility.notes: The Public Utilities Commission of Nevada's own 'Electric' utilities page confirms two PUCN-regulated electric utilities exist statewide — Sierra Pacific Power Company and Nevada Power Company — both doing business as 'NV Energy'; it does not itself state the county-level service boundary (the PUCN's own service-area maps are image-based and not text-extractable). Nevada Power Company is independently, historically documented as the Las Vegas-based utility serving the southern part of Nevada including Clark County (pre-2005, before its parent group renamed to NV Energy), which is the basis for attributing Las Vegas to this specific entity rather than Sierra Pacific Power Company (the northern-Nevada/Reno-area entity).

value.name: Nevada Power Company d/b/a NV Energy
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Las Vegas this session; Nevada Power Company is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Las Vegas Department of Building & Safety
permit_authority.notes: Nevada has no statewide residential building code or statewide solar-permitting rule — permitting authority sits entirely with the local city or county building department. Las Vegas is an incorporated city with its own Building & Safety Department (distinct from unincorporated Clark County, which is a separate AHJ not covered by this record).

interconnection_url.notes: NV Energy's own net-metering application materials (PowerClerk Interconnect portal, its own handbook, and its RE-3 interconnection standard) could not be retrieved this session — nvenergy.com refused every connection attempt (ECONNREFUSED) via both the fetch tool and the browser tool, a genuine source-access block, not a content issue. The Public Utilities Commission of Nevada's own program page is used instead as the authoritative description of the net-metering framework Nevada Power Company operates under.

battery_programs.notes: No statewide Nevada battery/storage incentive program was found this session. NV Energy may offer its own utility-specific storage program, but its own site was inaccessible this session (see interconnection_url notes) — left null rather than guessed.

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Residential Photovoltaic (Solar) Permits' policy (effective 2024-02-15): these two documents are required for the same-day online issuance path (no energy storage/battery system, no ballasted mounting, licensed electrical contractor only). Systems with an ESS/battery or ballasted racking, or filed as an Owner/Builder permit, are routed to a full plan review instead — the City's own document does not itemize the full-review document list beyond 'submit for a full plan review,' so that path's exact document set is not recorded here.

value: A single combined inspection (Inspection #227) covers the photovoltaic installation — no separate structural or plan-review site visit is required for a standard PV-only system
Printed plans and electrical load calculations must be available onsite at the time of inspection even though the inspector primarily references the electronically-submitted plans
If the design changes after permit issuance, a Revision application with updated electrical plans/calculations must be submitted and approved before the inspection can proceed

value.notes: Per the City's own policy (effective 2024-02-15), a residential PV/solar permit without an energy storage system (ESS/battery) or ballasted mounting is eligible for same-day online issuance and inspection scheduling, provided the applicant is a licensed electrical contractor (owner/builder permits are excluded and require a full plan review). No day-count was stated for the full-plan-review path (battery/ballasted systems, or owner/builder permits).

value.program_or_pathway: Same-Day Online PV Permit (licensed electrical contractor, no battery/ballasted system) vs. standard Full Plan Review
other_conditions: Same-day online issuance requires a licensed electrical contractor — Owner/Builder permits are not eligible and must submit for a full plan review
Any system that includes an energy storage/battery system (ESS) or a ballasted mounting system is excluded from same-day issuance and requires a full plan review instead
Online permit applications are automatically voided by the City's system if permit fees are not paid within 10 days of submission
Separately, NV Energy's own net-metering program (via the PUCN) caps net-metered renewable systems at 25 kW — a utility interconnection limit, not a City permit-eligibility limit

permit_fees.notes: Extracted directly from the City's own published 2020 Building User Fees schedule (Table 3-D, effective July 1, 2021), whose 'Photovoltaic system' line item is an exact terminology match for residential solar PV permits, filed as a stand-alone electrical (MPE) permit. The example dollar figure ($314.00) shown in the City's separate step-by-step PV-permit walkthrough document is explicitly a screenshot of test/sample application data ('Test PV no plan'), not a real fee quote, and was not used here.

rebates.notes: No statewide Nevada solar income-tax-credit, sales-tax-exemption, or cash-rebate program was found this session — unlike Colorado, Arizona, Oregon, or New Mexico, Nevada does not appear to offer one at the state level (consistent with the mission's own pre-session DSIRE-based Nevada research note finding no dedicated statewide solar-permitting or incentive entry). Net metering (recorded separately in interconnection_url/eligibility_constraints) is Nevada's primary financial mechanism for residential solar, not a rebate.
